$comment: EOS — the nonprod OPERATING COMPANY -> eos_ops PARTITION KEY bindings.
THE KEY IS EVIDENCE, NOT AN OPERATOR GUESS. It is declared here and only here, so that no
reconciliation run can introduce a key from a command line, and no code can derive one. The CLI
that consumes this file accepts no key argument at all.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. eos_policy.tenant_operating_companies says WHICH COMPANIES a tenant may
operate as. eos_ops.*.operating_company_key says WHICH PARTITION an operational row belongs to.
They were never the same thing, and nonprod proves it rather than merely asserting it: the Sample
Company fixture carries operatingCompanyId 'taylor' with operatingCompanyKey 'sample-co-synthetic',
deliberately, so its rows are confined to a partition nothing else uses. Copying one field into the
other would assert an equality this repository explicitly denies.
TAYLOR'S KEY HAPPENS TO READ THE SAME AS ITS COMPANY ID, AND THAT IS A COINCIDENCE OF AUTHORING.
It is NOT an equality rule and must never be implemented as one. Code reads the binding row; a
resolver that returned the company id when no row existed would be inventing a partition.
SAMPLE COMPANY IS NOT BOUND HERE. 'sample-co-synthetic' is fixture data and stays outside the
governed business partition. Genuine Work Orders are never migrated into it.
VENTANA IS AUTHORIZED BUT UNKEYED, DELIBERATELY. The tenant may operate as Ventana, and a native
Ventana operational row must FAIL CLOSED until an explicit key binding is authored here. Supporting
a company conceptually and keying its partition are two separate decisions.
